$comment: Mutation-score floor for the Stryker gate (#74). stryker-config.json's thresholds.break MUST equal 'floor' — Stryker exits non-zero below it, failing the weekly stryker.yaml run, which auto-files an issue. Ratchet policy: the floor only moves UP, in a PR that shows the new sustained score; lowering it requires a written rationale in the same PR. History lives in this file's git log.

measured.environment: local win-x64, dotnet-stryker 4.16.0, Release unit suite (376 tests)

history.note: first real run (stryker.yaml had been a config-less no-op)

#176 pass: 18 behavioural killing tests (verify/recurse flags, exit codes, retention dir + boundary, report counts, filter order, sink defaults) + ignore-methods for Log*/WriteLine* — log-statement mutants are unassertable by design, excluding them turns the score into signal

#176 second pass after the v0.3.0 features dropped the score to 81.12 (below the 83 gate): 27 killing tests - verifier tar-walk isolation (valid compression wrapping non-tar bytes), ctor null-guards, exact retry-attempt counts, skip-mode continuation, byte-count/OriginalSize sums, uniquifier counter progression, directory-entry extraction, expected-size-zero boundary

survivorProfile: 95 survivors + 4 no-coverage - dominated by ConfigureAwait(false)->true boolean flips (equivalent under xunit: no SynchronizationContext) and leaveOpen argument booleans (disposal semantics indistinguishable in context), plus a few unreachable-by-construction branches (root-directory bundle sources, whitespace folder names). Raising the floor past ~88 means hunting those case-by-case; check the HTML report from the weekly stryker.yaml artifact.
